AkkLove LAOS4-06 (P424004) – translation (Wasserman 2016)

Web: https://oracc.museum.upenn.edu/akklove/P424004/html

Project translation extracted from the ORACC HTML view (rank 3 in our hierarchy; consult only after our own reading).
Each paragraph: [first label – last label of the transliteration lines it translates] text. "## " = section heading.

[o i 1] Where is my loved one? He is so dear!
[o i 2] And does he bear his fruit?
[o i 3] ...
[o i 4] Like apples of the ripening period (or: the month of Simān(?))
[o i 5] Filled with joy is the bed of [my lover(?)]
[o i 6] My love had to go out to the steppe,
[o i 7] (while) I spend (here) the night.
[o i 8] I embrace my delight,
[o i 9] but the dove rose aloft.
[o i 11] My love of the steppe, may the trappers return (him) back to me!
[o i 13] You will embrace my delights.
[o i 14] May the gardener bring (him) to me!
[o i 16] I have thrown my coop on the young man,
[o i 17] so that I may catch the dove;
[o i 19] (The coop) of my delights Nanāya(?) will fill for me.
[o i 21] Indeed, he is loved,
[o i 22] and the short friend(?) [...]
[o i 23] The minister [...] the peg.
[o i 24] ... to remember [...]
[o i 25] [...] your(f.) [lo]ved one [...]
[o i 26] ...

[r iv 6'] An omen for your well-being and your everlasting life!
[r iv 8'] May Ištar grant to you, Ammī-ditāna, her life anew!
[r iv 10'] May the loved one be in your heart, (may) you cherish her favorably!
[r iv 12'] Learn(pl.), learn(pl.) and ask one another:
[r iv 13'] “(Though) its beginning is sighs of woe, still young is my love!”.
[r iv 15'] Its antiphon.
[r iv 16'] 4 irtum songs
[r iv 17'] (Of) the series “Where is my loved one, he is so dear”.
